proposed_widenings.name: FeatRecord + FeatMechanics family
proposed_widenings.justification: UnitRecord has no 'feat' kind. types.ts only defines SpellRecord, ClassFeatureRecord, and MasteryRecord. Feats require a new top-level record kind with its own mechanics header (at minimum: no class/level requirement, may bundle ASI + active rider). The TAXONOMY has feat_root as an atom but no surface family corresponds to it.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Epic Boon Feat (Prerequisite: Level 19+) — the feat kind is not representable in UnitRecord at all.

proposed_widenings.name: force_hit (or modify_roll_outcome: miss_to_hit)
proposed_widenings.justification: Peerless Aim converts a missed attack roll into a hit without rerolling. This is distinct from modify_roll_reroll (reroll keeping higher/lower), modify_roll_substitute (replace with a fixed numeric value), and modify_roll_numeric (add a die/flat bonus). It operates on the resolved outcome (miss), not on the roll value itself, and overrides the outcome to hit. No v4 atom covers this.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you miss with an attack roll, you can hit instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.

proposed_widenings.name: modify_ability_score
proposed_widenings.justification: Ability Score Increase is the canonical ASI rider shared by most feats. TAXONOMY §12 already records this as a known deferred atom ('modify_ability_score as a runtime effect versus as pre-runtime character state'). It is out-of-scope for the current atom inventory but is required to represent the ASI benefit of this feat.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 30.

notes: Two independent blockers. Primary: no FeatRecord kind exists — the surface cannot represent a feat at all, so no honest encoding is possible. Secondary: even with a FeatRecord, Peerless Aim requires a 'force hit' effect atom that has no v4 equivalent, and ASI requires modify_ability_score which is explicitly deferred. The Peerless Aim rider also has an on_miss_window trigger shape, but the miss-outcome-to-hit conversion has no target effect atom in v4. The Rogue's Stroke of Luck (L20) exercises a similar shape; both would need the same widening.
